info.title: Beacon server
info.description:
The Beacon server's REST API. The server verifies identity and signatures, and never judges a gameplay claim. Every state-changing op is a signed `OpEnvelope` POSTed over REST; the socket.io live and map channels are server-to-client events, described in the API reference rather than here. Some routes are opt-in capabilities that answer 404 while their setting is off.

## Refusals

A refusal carries the JSON body `{ ok: false, error, message?, fields? }` (the `Refusal` schema), where `error` is a code a client can act on. A path no route serves answers 404 `unknownRoute`, a request body over the server's limit answers 413 `tooLarge`, and a body the server cannot read answers `invalid`: a 400 for one that is not JSON, a 415 for a charset or an encoding it does not take. A reply without that body, such as a reverse proxy's error page, is not the server's refusal.

## Signed requests

Every request that changes state, and every signed read, carries a signed `OpEnvelope`: the op name and its `params`, the acting account (`actor`), the device key that signs (`device`) with the account's authorization of that key (`auth`), a `nonce`, the issue time, and `sig`, an Ed25519 signature by `device` over the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of the envelope without `sig`. The server answers a bad signature with 401 `badsig`, and an envelope issued outside its replay window with 400 `clockSkew`. A game's envelope names its game slug, and the operator routes take envelopes from a key on the server's admin allowlist. The envelope is the JSON body, except on `POST /media`, which wraps the envelope beside the bytes, and on `POST /places/admin/atlas/upload`, which takes the envelope in a header. `POST /profiles` takes a profile doc, which the account signs itself.

Each signed route's request body fixes `op` to the op names the route takes and points `params` at the schema the server parses them with. `POST /rooms/{id}/ops` lists its op names only: the params of a room op are what the room's policy says they are.

The signature is computed on the client, so this page cannot send a signed request. Use the client SDK (`@beaconsgg/client-sdk`), which builds and signs envelopes, and the signing guide in the Beacon documentation. The unsigned GET routes can be tried from here.

get.summary: Reverse-geocode a geohash to a neighborhood, city, state and country label
get.description: Opt-in capability (`BEACON_GEOCODE`): routes 404 when disabled. Proxies a geocoder (Nominatim) with a server-side cache. The `neighborhood` field is omitted for a cache cell coarser than geohash-7 (about 150 m), whose center can sit in a different neighborhood than the point that asked, so the precision of the answer follows the precision of the geohash you send.

400.description: The `geohash` is not a valid geohash cell (`invalid`).

503.description: The upstream geocoder did not answer (`upstreamUnavailable`).

get.summary: The curated vocabulary of categories and their subcategories
get.description: Opt-in capability (`BEACON_PLACES`): routes 404 when disabled. What a contribution UI renders its pickers from, and what `places.propose` fences new-place submissions to. Slugs are **namespaced per category**: always read the pair. Derived from the server's tag map, so it changes only when an operator edits it; freely cacheable. Display labels are a game concern.

get.summary: Places from the server's owned dataset within the queried cells
get.description: Opt-in capability (`BEACON_PLACES`): routes 404 when disabled. Serves the curated place dataset, always from the server's own store, never proxied. Multi-cell CSV query (the discovery shape) with optional taxonomy `categories` filter. Keyset-paginated: a full page returns a `cursor`; re-query with `?cursor=<cursor>` (same `cells`/`categories`) to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: keyset cursor: a prior page's `cursor` (a place ULID)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: page size (clamped to the server max)

parameters.name: spread
parameters.description: `1` samples one page evenly across the cells instead of taking the lowest ids. A spread page has no `cursor`, and a request may not send both.

400.description: A query parameter is invalid: a cell's charset or precision, the count of cells or categories, a `cursor` that is not a ULID, a `limit` that is not a positive integer, or a `spread` other than `1` or beside a `cursor` (`invalid`).

get.summary: One place with its full geometry and provenance
get.description: Pass `?contributors=1` to include the DIDs of players whose approved contribution to this place asked to be credited. Opt-in because `PlaceDetail` is strict: a client that doesn't ask never receives the key, so the field could ship ahead of the apps that read it.

400.description: The `unique` is not a ULID (`invalid`).

404.description: The places capability is off (`unknownRoute`), or no active place has that `unique` (`unknownPlace`).

Marks every live record of the named source gone as a durable run: the migration path for legacy connector residue (`osm`), refused for the living inputs (`admin`, `contrib`, `list:*`, `atlas:*`). Run it after importing the Atlas volumes that cover the region, so adoption has already carried place identity. Idempotent by envelope nonce.

post.summary: Propose a new place, or descriptor fields for one that exists
post.description: Opt-in capability (`BEACON_PLACES_PROPOSALS`): routes 404 when disabled. A **signed player** request from any DID (this is not the operator surface), rate-limited per DID and capped on unreviewed backlog. Records a `pending` proposal and publishes **nothing**: an operator must approve it before it reaches any read path. A new place needs a valid `(category, subcategory)` pair; an improvement may only add `name`/`description`/`website`/`media`. Referenced media must already be stored on THIS server. Idempotent by envelope nonce.

400.description: The body is not JSON, the envelope or its params are malformed, or the op is not one this route takes (`invalid`); `fields` names the keys this server does not know when those are the only problem. An `issuedAt` more than five minutes from the server's clock answers `clockSkew`. The category pair is not curated (`invalidPair`), the place is unknown (`unknownPlace`), or the media is not stored here (`unknownMedia`).

403.description: The server blocked the account (`denied`), or the account revoked the signing device (`deviceRevoked`). 409.description: The account has as many proposals awaiting review as the server allows (`tooManyPending`). Not retryable: it clears when an operator reviews one. A signed read already used the nonce (`replayed`).

error.description:
The refusal's code. These are the codes this server sends; a newer server may add codes, so read an unknown one as a refusal you have no special handling for.

- `badsig`: The signature does not verify.
- `invalid`: The body, the envelope or its params are malformed. `fields` names the keys this server does not know when those keys are the only problem.
- `unknownRoom`: The room is gone or never existed.
- `expired`: The room has closed.
- `denied`: The caller may not do this. The account is blocked, the room's policy does not allow the op for this player, or the signer is not on `BEACON_ADMINS`.
- `gameNotAdmitted`: This server does not admit the envelope's game, or the envelope names no game.
- `phase`: The room's current phase does not allow the op.
- `full`: The room has reached its capacity.
- `gone`: The item was already taken or claimed.
- `empty`: The room has nothing to take.
- `locked`: The time window is not open. This server answers `phase` for that case instead.
- `rateLimited`: The caller went over a rate limit.
- `stale`: The envelope's `baseVersion` is no longer the room's version, or a profile is older.
- `deviceRevoked`: The account revoked the signing device.
- `clockSkew`: The envelope's `issuedAt` is more than five minutes from the server's clock.
- `gameNotAccepted`: This room does not open the op to the envelope's game.
- `notMember`: The server's `accessLevel` is `request` or `private`, and the signer is not a member. `denied` to a client that has not declared this code.
- `unknownRoute`: No route serves the path, or the capability that serves the path is turned off. A 404 that names a missing thing (`unknownPlace`, `unknownMedia`, `unknownProposal`, `unknownRun`, `noAbout`) is `unknownRoute` to a client that has not declared that code.
- `unknownPlace`: No active place has that `unique`.
- `unknownMedia`: No media has that hash, or a proposal names media this server does not store.
- `unknownProposal`: No proposal has that id.
- `unknownRun`: No run has that id.
- `noAbout`: The operator has set no about text.
- `tooLarge`: The body, or a value in the body, is over the server's limit.
- `replayed`: The nonce was used before by a signed read.
- `conflict`: The server's state refuses the request: another account holds the room id, or a backup or restore is already running.
- `writeLocked`: The server is locked read-only. Try again after the `Retry-After` interval.
- `invalidPair`: The `subcategory` is not a curated slug of the `category`.
- `tooManyPending`: The account already has as many proposals awaiting review as the server allows. A state refusal (409): it clears when an operator reviews one, so retrying does not help.
- `unsupportedType`: This server does not take the media type.
- `hashMismatch`: The bytes do not match the signed hash.
- `metadataPresent`: The image carries EXIF or GPS metadata. Strip the metadata and upload again.
- `quotaExceeded`: The account's media quota or the server's storage is full.
- `upstreamUnavailable`: The geocoder this server proxies did not answer.
- `unknownProfile`: No profile for that account is published to this server.

Refusal.description: A refusal. The server sends `deviceRevoked`, `clockSkew`, `gameNotAccepted`, `notMember` only to a client that declares the code in the `beacon-understands` header, as `code:<name>`. Any other client gets the older code in its place: `denied` for `deviceRevoked`, `invalid` for `clockSkew`, `denied` for `gameNotAccepted`, `denied` for `notMember`, and `unknownRoute` for a 404 `unknownPlace`, `unknownMedia`, `unknownProposal`, `unknownRun`, `noAbout`. Every other code goes to every client.

TooLarge.description: The body is over the server's size limit (`tooLarge`).

UnsupportedBody.description: The server does not take the body's charset or content encoding (`invalid`).

WriteLocked.description: The server is locked read-only (`writeLocked`). The answer carries a `Retry-After` header.

WriteRateLimited.description: The client went over the write rate limit (`rateLimited`).

ReadRateLimited.description: The client went over the read rate limit (`rateLimited`).

SignedReadRateLimited.description: The client went over the signed-read rate limit (`rateLimited`).
